rules.title: Statewide residential rent increase cap
rules.requirement: For covered residential rental property, an owner may not increase rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the applicable cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower. If the same tenant remains in the unit, rent may not be increased in more than two increments during that 12-month period.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10%; no more than two increases in 12 months for same tenant
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories owned and operated by higher-education or K-12 institutions; housing subject to valid local rent or price control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years unless the housing is a mobilehome; qualifying separately alienable residential property with required notice and non-corporate/non-REIT ownership; certain owner-occupied two-unit single-structure properties where neither unit is an ADU or JADU; or a homeowner of a mobilehome.
rules.penalty: An owner who demands, accepts, receives, or retains rent above the maximum is liable in a civil action for injunctive relief, excess-rent damages, discretionary reasonable attorney’s fees and costs, and, for willful or oppressive, fraudulent, or malicious conduct, up to treble damages; the Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel may enforce and seek injunctive relief.
rules.interaction: The section excludes housing already subject to valid local rent or price control with lower annual increases and states that it does not expand or limit local authority to regulate rents consistently with Chapter 2.7 commencing with Section 1954.50. Yields to a stricter local ordinance where one covers the unit (LA-RENT-01, SF-RENT-01, BER-RENT-01, SA-RENT-01); reported as superseded at those addresses.

rules.requirement_es: Para una propiedad residencial en alquiler cubierta por esta regla, el propietario no puede aumentar la renta en cualquier período de 12 meses en más de 5% más el cambio aplicable por costo de vida, o 10%, lo que sea menor. rules.title: Statewide just-cause eviction protections for residential tenancies
rules.requirement: After the tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential rental for 12 months, the owner may terminate only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written notice; if additional adult tenants join, protection applies when all tenants have 12 months or one has 24 months. For no-fault terminations, the owner must provide relocation assistance or a final-month rent waiver equal to one month’s rent, and curable lease violations require a chance to cure first.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; if additional adult tenants join, all tenants 12 months or one tenant 24 months; no-fault relocation assistance or rent waiver = 1 month’s rent
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to qualifying local just-cause ordinances as described in subdivision (i); transient and tourist hotel occupancy; housing accommodations in specified nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, licensed elder care, or adult residential facilities; dormitories owned and operated by schools or higher-education institutions; housing where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with the owner who maintains a principal residence there; single-family owner-occupied residences renting or leasing no more than two units or bedrooms, including an ADU or JADU, and mobilehomes; owner-occupied two-unit properties in one structure if neither unit is an ADU or JADU; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years unless it is a mobilehome; qualifying separately alienable residential property with required notice; specified affordable housing; and homeowners of mobilehomes.
rules.penalty: An owner’s failure to comply renders the written termination notice void. An owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, discretionary reasonable attorney’s fees and costs, up to three times actual damages for willful or oppressive, fraudulent, or malicious conduct, possible punitive damages, and injunctive relief sought by the Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel.
rules.interaction: Residential real property is not subject to both this section and a local just-cause ordinance; qualifying pre-September 1, 2019 local ordinances and more protective later local ordinances apply instead, while less protective local ordinances adopted after September 1, 2019 are not enforceable unless this section is repealed. rules.title: California residential security deposit limits and return rules
rules.requirement: For residential rentals, a landlord generally may not demand or receive a security deposit greater than one month’s rent, must use it only for authorized purposes such as unpaid rent, tenant-caused damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and necessary cleaning, and must return the remainder with an itemized statement no later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates. Tenants may request an initial inspection before move-out, and bad-faith retention or claims against the deposit can expose the landlord to statutory damages.
rules.key_value: 1 month’s rent; qualifying small-landlord exception up to 2 months’ rent; return/accounting within 21 calendar days; bad-faith damages up to 2x security
rules.exemptions: The one-month cap does not prohibit an advance payment of at least six months’ rent if the lease term is six months or longer, does not preclude a mutual agreement for tenant-requested structural, decorative, furnishing, or similar alterations, and does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. Initial-inspection requirements do not apply when the tenancy is terminated under subdivision (2), (3), or (4) of Code of Civil Procedure § 1161. Certain documentation requirements do not apply if repair and cleaning deductions together do not exceed $125 or if the tenant validly waives them, subject to later tenant request rights.
rules.penalty: A landlord who in bad faith claims or retains security, or demands replacement security in violation of the section, may be liable for statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages; a landlord who in bad faith fails to comply with the 21-day return/itemization subdivision is not entitled to claim any amount of the security.

rules.title: Residential rental application screening fees
rules.requirement: A California landlord may charge a residential rental applicant only an application screening fee that does not exceed the landlord’s actual authorized screening costs and the statutory cap, adjusted annually for CPI. The landlord must not charge when no unit is available, must follow one of the statute’s fee/refund screening processes, provide an itemized receipt, return unused amounts, and provide any consumer credit report obtained to the applicant within seven days of receiving it.

rules.requirement: For covered housing spaces, a landlord may not increase rent at lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy by more than the stated CPI formula, capped at 4%, and may not increase rent more than that in any consecutive twelve-month period regardless of vacancy, new tenant, or ownership change. ancillary.title: Unconscionable Rent Increase
ancillary.requirement: A residential rent increase may be treated as unconscionable if it is exceedingly harsh or unreasonable, exceeds the increase in the landlord’s expenses, and is not comparable to rents charged at similar properties. For properties with a redevelopment agreement or financial agreement, rent that exceeds the approved pro-forma is per se unconscionable.
ancillary.key_value: Exceedingly harsh or unreasonable; exceeds landlord’s expenses; not comparable to similar properties
ancillary.exemptions: Residential units statutorily exempt from Rent Control pursuant to N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1-84.6 and units controlled and governed by HUD are excluded.
ancillary.interaction: The definition states that it does not apply to units statutorily exempt from rent control under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1-84.6 or to units controlled and governed by HUD.

ancillary.title: Protection from retaliatory eviction and condo/co-op conversion eviction for eligible senior and disabled tenants
ancillary.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession as retaliation for a tenant’s effort to secure or enforce rights under the Newark rent control chapter. The ordinance also provides an application process for senior citizen and disabled tenants seeking protected tenancy status from eviction due to condominium or cooperative conversion.
ancillary.penalty: The Rent Control Board may impose a monetary penalty not to exceed $500 for a violation of any provision of the chapter, after notice and an opportunity for hearing.
ancillary.interaction: The protected-tenancy provision states that eligibility determinations are guided by the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22.
ancillary.quoted_span: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.
ancillary.law_name: Newark Rent Control Regulations Retaliatory Eviction and Protected Tenancy Provisions

ancillary.title: Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources required when ending a tenancy
ancillary.requirement: When a Boston landlord serves a Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal or expiration, the landlord must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time. Landlords and foreclosing owners must also send required notices and a certificate of compliance/service to Boston’s Office of Housing Stability.
ancillary.key_value: Notice required at the same time as Notice to Quit; 2nd and subsequent offenses: $300 per day
ancillary.exemptions: The only exempt properties are residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, and residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
ancillary.penalty: Violations are enforced by the Inspectional Services Department: 1st offense warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day. The FAQ states that a violation does not halt the eviction process.
ancillary.interaction: The document does not state any interaction with other state or local eviction rules; it states that failure to provide the notice does not halt the eviction process.
ancillary.quoted_span:

ancillary.law_name: Housing Stability Notification Act
